To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) neural circuits form by a series of processes that are highly regulated and that are dependent on a small number of key molecules, many of which are used for multiple functions; (2) the formation of neural circuits is essential for proper behavior, and the disruption of any of these processes results in a variety of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders; and (3), the study of these molecules in small circuits and defined processes is providing new insight into the molecular mechanisms of circuit formation, but

(1) the molecular mechanisms that regulate neural circuit formation are complex; (2) these mechanisms are not unique, but are shared with a number of other processes; (3) the molecular mechanisms underlying neural circuit formation are conserved from Drosophila to humans.
